name: application-medication-schedule-list
title: Medication Schedule List
description: Medication dose schedule with time, medication/dosage, and either a resolved Taken/Skipped badge or Take/Skip actions per dose.
useWhen: Showing a patient's or user's daily medication schedule with clear times and dosage information.
Users need to mark each dose as taken or skipped, with the row visually resolving once logged.
You want past/logged doses to look distinctly resolved (dimmed, badge) from upcoming ones (still showing actions).
avoidWhen: Doses aren't user-loggable (a read-only prescription list) — drop the action buttons and show only time/medication/dosage.
You need a general-purpose task checklist unrelated to medication — a plain checklist component is simpler and avoids implying clinical semantics.
This is patient-facing clinical software requiring regulatory-grade audit trails — this is a UI pattern only, not a substitute for a validated medication-adherence system.
responsiveBehavior: Time, medication/dosage, and the trailing badge/actions sit in a single flex row with a fixed-width time column, keeping doses vertically scannable at any width.
accessibility: Resolved doses show real text status ("Taken", "Skipped"), not color alone, and reduce the row's visual weight rather than hiding it.
Take and Skip are separate, explicitly labeled buttons rather than a single ambiguous toggle.
Dosage and quantity are both present as text so users can confirm the exact dose before logging it, not just the medication name.

variants.title: Medication Schedule List
variants.description: Four doses: one taken, two pending with Take/Skip actions, and one skipped and dimmed.
accessibility: Logging a dose transitions real per-row state from pending to taken/skipped, replacing the action buttons with a status badge.

variants.title: Medication Schedule List (Dark)
variants.description: Medication schedule list adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Status badge and dimmed-row colors are tuned to meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark surface.
